info.name: Home Maintenance API
info.description: Domain-organized collection. Set {{base_url}}; login/register auto-saves {{token}} for authed requests.

request.description: Validates the phone and sends a 4-digit OTP. In dev (SMS_DRIVER=log) read it from storage/logs/laravel.log.

Consumes the OTP and returns a short-lived, single-use verification ticket (auto-saved to {{register_ticket}}). Does NOT create the account — feed the ticket into Register — Client or Technician > Register Technician.

formdata.description: Optional profile photo (image only, max 4 MB).

request.description: Multipart form-data. Redeems {{register_ticket}} (from Verify OTP), creates a client + wallet, returns a token (auto-saved to {{token}}). profile_photo is optional (image only) — attach a file to include it.

Permanently closes the signed-in account: confirm with the current password. Revokes every token, takes a technician offline, and soft-deletes the record (login is then blocked). Requires the bearer {{token}}.
Consumes the reset OTP and returns a short-lived, single-use ticket (auto-saved to {{reset_ticket}}). Feed it into Password — Reset.
Redeems {{reset_ticket}} (from Password — Verify OTP), sets the new password, and revokes all sessions.
Update the signed-in user's display name and optional profile image URL.

Admin-only. Credits the platform guarantee fund (the wallet that pays substitute technicians for warranty visits). Immediately retries any warranty payouts that were waiting on funds. Requires an admin bearer {{token}}.
Manual top-up: transfer to the account from /app-settings, then upload the receipt. Creates a PENDING top-up (no credit until an admin approves).
The caller's own top-up requests (manual + instant).
Manual top-ups awaiting review.
Approve + credit the wallet. Optional amount corrects to what the receipt shows.
Decline a manual top-up; nothing is credited.
Stream the uploaded transfer receipt.

Register (or move) an FCM device token for the authenticated user. Call on login/app-start and whenever the token changes. platform: android | ios | web. updateOrCreate on the token — re-registering updates instead of duplicating, and a token moves to the new user on a shared device.
Remove a device token (call on logout). Only deletes a token owned by the current user.

Mints a Firebase custom token for the signed-in user (uid = app user id). The app exchanges it via signInWithCustomToken() to read/write the Realtime Database live-location node. Requires the bearer {{token}}.

Public (no auth) — powers the guest home screen. Returns active top-level service categories, each with active children nested. Every category includes icon_url (an Iconify Material Design SVG, e.g. https://api.iconify.design/mdi/flash.svg) and guide_price.
Public. Client-readable app settings (fees, windows, radii) the apps need at runtime.
The platform's physical offices/branches.
PLANNED — the authenticated client's saved addresses.
PLANNED — create a new client address.
PLANNED — update an address by id.
PLANNED — delete an address by id.
A single saved address by id (must belong to the caller).

formdata.description: Required only when type=scheduled. A future ISO datetime, e.g. 2026-08-20T14:00:00Z.
Optional flaw photos (max 3, images only). Enable the extra rows to attach several.

request.description:
Multipart form-data. Creates an order and holds the inspection fee in escrow. Requires a funded wallet (top up first). Auto-saves the new id to {{order_id}}. For a scheduled order, set type=scheduled and enable scheduled_at (a future ISO datetime).

operation_id is an idempotency token: reuse the SAME value to retry safely (a repeat returns the same order, the fee is held once). {{$guid}} generates a fresh one on each send — pin it to a fixed value to test idempotency.

photos[] are optional flaw photos (max 3, images only). Attach files to the photos[] rows; enable the extra rows to send more than one.
Streams a private order photo (flaw/closure/dispute) by id, if the caller is a party to the order.

formdata.description: Optional profile photo (image only, max 4 MB).

request.description: Multipart form-data. First run Auth > Register — Start (phone 0913333333) then Register — Verify OTP so {{register_ticket}} is set. Attach id_front, id_back, selfie image files. Redeems the ticket, creates a technician (status=pending) and logs you in (saves {{token}}). profile_photo is optional (image only).
Admin only. Log in as an admin (Auth > Login) so {{token}} is an admin token, set {{technician_id}}, then approve → status active.

Admin only. Sanction for reliability failures: status → probation with a capped daily order limit and taken offline. Also resolves that tech's open flags with outcome=suspended (+ optional note). Re-approve to reinstate.
Admin only. status → banned and taken offline (removed from anywhere). Also resolves that tech's open flags with outcome=banned (+ optional note).
Lift a ban — restarts the technician in a fresh probation trial.
Admin only. The queue of open reliability offenses (no-show / withdrawal) awaiting assessment, newest first. Saves the first id to {{flag_id}}.
Admin only. Marks a flag reviewed (dismiss / acknowledge) with an optional note. For an actual sanction, use suspend/ban (which also clears the tech's open flags).
Open dispatch offers for the logged-in technician. Auto-saves the first offer's id to {{offer_id}}.
Atomically take the job. 409 if the order was already taken or the offer expired.
Decline and re-offer the order to the next nearest technician.
Progress toward promotion out of probation (completed orders + rating vs the thresholds).
Lightweight location heartbeat — the app sends it every ~3 min or ~300 m while available. Refreshes the dispatch snapshot + its freshness stamp so a stale position can't misroute urgent orders.
Save (or replace) the technician's Sham Cash payout account. Required before a withdrawal can be requested. account_number is exactly 16 digits (stored encrypted); account_holder_name max 255.
Initial quote after arriving on-site. multipart/form-data: each part's photo is uploaded as a file (parts[i][image]); the server stores it privately and returns image_url as a streaming URL.
Client or assigned technician lists the order's quotes. Auto-saves the newest quote id to {{quote_id}}.
Client approves -> holds the repair fee in escrow and moves the order to in_progress. 422 if the wallet can't cover it.
Client rejects -> order closes as inspection_only.
Add-on quote for extra work found mid-repair. multipart/form-data: part photos uploaded as files (parts[i][image]).
Assigned technician marks on-site arrival. The server verifies the GPS is within arrival_radius_meters (default 50m) of the order location; 422 if out of range. Required before a quote can be sent.

Assigned technician pauses an in-progress order to source a part (in_progress -> waiting_for_parts). Stamps a deadline (parts_wait_max_hours, default 72h); an overdue wait is flagged for admin review. The order stays assigned.
Assigned technician returns with the part and resumes the job (waiting_for_parts -> in_progress).
Technician signals work is done and attaches 1–3 completion photos. multipart/form-data: attach one or more photos[] files (min 1, max 3).
Client reads their active closure code and shares it with the technician in person. Auto-saves it to {{closure_code}} for convenience. 404 if the technician hasn't requested closure yet.
Assigned technician submits the code to complete the job. Order -> completed and a 48h dispute window opens; held funds release automatically after it (release cron).

formdata.value: The tap is leaking again the next day.

request.description: Client raises a dispute (multipart/form-data). Valid in two moments: during the closure review window (order still in_progress, tech has requested closure) to catch on-site damage, OR during the 48h held window after completion. Order -> disputed, which freezes the release cron. reason: fault_returned | home_damage | different_part | other. photos[] is OPTIONAL — up to 5 image evidence files (jpg/jpeg/png/webp, ≤4MB each), returned in data.photos and viewable via /api/order-photos/{id}. Auto-saves the new id to {{dispute_id}}.

Admin-only. resolution: full_refund | partial_refund | release_to_technician (warranty_order not implemented yet). refund_amount is required for partial_refund and is refunded to the client FIFO across held payments; the remainder is released to the technician (minus commission). Order -> resolved.
Disputes visible to the caller (client's own, or an admin's full queue).
Client rates a completed (or resolved) order once. cleanliness/quality/price_rating are 1-5. A low price_rating (<=2) sets price_anomaly_flag server-side. 409 if not completed or already reviewed.

Client claims the warranty within warranty_until. Spawns a same-technician, zero-labor warranty order (kind=warranty, parent_order_id set, status in_progress). 409 if the warranty expired, order isn't completed, or a warranty visit already exists. Saves the new order id to {{warranty_order_id}}.

Client cancels. Pending -> full inspection-fee refund. Accepted/Scheduled -> late cancel: the tech keeps cancel_fee_share (30%), the rest is refunded and the appointment is freed. 409 once the order is in_progress or beyond.

Assigned tech drops an accepted/scheduled job. Frees the slot, returns the order to Pending and re-dispatches to the next technician (inspection fee stays held). 409 if the job is already in progress.

Assigned tech reports the client was absent on-site (order must be accepted / tech on-site). The system does NOT pay out — no status change, the inspection fee stays held. It raises a client-no-show claim for admin review; an admin then resolves it. One open claim per order.

Client reports a suspected technician no-show (order must be accepted). The system does NOT act — no refund, no status change. It raises a flag for admin review; an admin then resolves it. One open report per order.

Admin resolves a reported no-show (technician OR client), routing by the open claim on the order. outcome=dismissed → nothing moves, the order carries on. outcome=confirmed → a technician no-show refunds the client in full; a client no-show releases the full inspection fee to the technician. Either way the order closes as no_show and the flag is upheld.

Technician cash-out — amount only. The payout goes to the technician's saved Sham Cash account (set it first via PUT /technician/sham-cash-account). Reserves the amount (available -> held). Guards: >= min_withdrawal_amount, <= available, one at a time, blocked during an open dispute, and blocked if no Sham Cash account is saved.
The technician's own withdrawal requests.
Stream the payout receipt the admin uploaded.
Withdrawals awaiting payout.
Mark paid + upload the payout receipt. Reserved funds leave the ledger.
Decline the payout; the reserved funds return to available.
Stream the payout receipt for the record.
The caller's bell notifications, newest first (paginated). Pass ?status=unread to filter.
Unread notifications only.
Unread count for the bell badge.
Mark a single notification read (idempotent; must be yours).
Mark every unread notification read.
The order's chat thread (newest first, paginated). Client, assigned tech, or admin.
Send text and/or an image to the other party. Allowed only while the order is active (locks read-only once finished).

formdata.description: Optional image (either text or image required).

request.description: Mark the other party's messages as read.
Stream a chat image (participant or admin).
